title: Throwing a stoneware ramekin set
subtitle: Four matching stoneware ramekins , oven-safe at cone 6 , thrown to consistent dimensions
excerpt: Four stoneware ramekins, each 60 mm tall and 80 mm in diameter, thrown to matching dimensions from smooth stoneware. The challenge is consistency: four identical small cylinders from the same clay batch, all within 3 mm of each other in height and rim diameter. Oven-safe after cone 6 firing.
sourceNotes: Stoneware ramekin set throwing pattern derived from first principles.

glossaryTerms.definition: The stage at which each ramekin is stiff enough to trim without distorting
First firing to cone 06 (approx 1000 degrees C)
Pyrometric measure of heat-work. Cone 6 is approx 1220 degrees C , standard stoneware glaze-fire temperature
Trimmed base ridge; keeps the ramekin base from showing glaze crawl on the shelf

content.text: Silica dust is the chronic studio hazard. Silicosis is irreversible. Mix wet whenever possible. Wear a P100 respirator any time raw glaze powders are open. Wet-clean only: no sweeping, no dry sanding indoors. Adequate ventilation when firing. Do not open a hot kiln below 80 degrees C.

The ramekin set is an exercise in matched production throwing. Weigh each ball of clay before sitting at the wheel so every ramekin starts with the same mass. Use calipers to measure rim diameter and the needle tool to measure height after each piece. The goal is a set of four that could be stacked in a restaurant kitchen.
Throw four cylinders to matching dimensions
Weigh and wedge four 280 g balls of smooth stoneware. Keep them covered until needed to prevent uneven drying.

For each ball, centre on the wheel head. Open to a 50 mm floor. Pull walls in two to three passes to reach 60 mm height and 80 mm rim diameter. Walls should be 7-8 mm thick. The ramekin form is a straight cylinder with a very slight outward flare at the rim.
After each ramekin, measure height with the needle tool and rim diameter with the calipers. Record the numbers or mark a stick gauge. The fourth ramekin should match the first within 3 mm.
Wire off each ramekin and allow all four to dry to leather-hard together.
Trim foot-rings
At
leather-hard
, centre each ramekin upside-down and trim a
foot-ring
4 mm tall using the loop tool. Remove excess clay from inside the foot-ring to match the wall thickness of the sides.
Bisque and glaze
Allow to reach bone-dry.
Bisque
fire to

06 (approx 1000 degrees C).

Glaze inside and outside each ramekin with two to three brush coats. Use the same number of coats on each so glaze thickness is consistent across the set. Clean all glaze from the foot-ring and base. Glaze-fire to cone 6 (1220 degrees C).

rows.problem: Ramekins vary more than 3 mm in height
rows.cause: Clay balls were not weighed consistently, or more water was used on some pieces
rows.fix: For the next batch, weigh every ball on a scale to within 5 g. Measure after each pull and adjust before wiring off.

rows.cause: Not enough pulling passes or insufficient pressure during pulling
rows.fix: Add a third pull-pass, using less water. The goal is 7-8 mm walls, not 12-15 mm.
